description: Profile Qwen3-1.7B on both vLLM and SGLang with Proton profiler, analyze kernel-level performance differences with proton-viewer, and produce a detailed comparison report
instructions: Use shadow context + tree data as primary Proton config (lowest overhead)
vLLM profiling uses --profiler-config JSON with proton backend
SGLang profiling uses python -m sglang.profiler with --proton flag or proton CLI wrapper
SGLang default port is 30000, vLLM default port is 8000
Workload params must be identical across frameworks for fair comparison
Make clear and simple code design for ease of understanding
Write docstring and inline comments for every method
Only write absolutely necessary code, avoid redundant code, keep codebase clean
Avoid fallbacks and try-catch — fail early to discover issues at the shallow surface
Do not include claude as co-author in commit message
Do not include US-00X in commit message, follow vLLM commit message style

userStories.title: vLLM offline batch profiling script
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want a script that profiles vLLM offline batch inference with Qwen3-1.7B using Proton so I have a baseline for comparison.
acceptanceCriteria: Script at scripts/profiling/comparison/vllm_offline.sh
Activates ~/vllm/.venv before running
Uses vllm bench latency with --profiler-config JSON containing proton_context=shadow, proton_data=tree, proton_hook=triton
Default workload: batch_size=8, input_len=1024, output_len=256, seed=42
All params configurable via CLI args (--model, --batch-size, --input-len, --output-len, --seed)
Output goes to profiling_output/comparison/vllm/offline/
Validates .hatchet output files with proton-viewer
Prints summary of output files on completion
Script runs successfully and produces valid .hatchet files

userStories.title: SGLang offline batch profiling script
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want a script that profiles SGLang offline batch inference with Qwen3-1.7B using the same workload as vLLM.
acceptanceCriteria: Script at scripts/profiling/comparison/sglang_offline.sh
Activates ~/sglang/.venv before running
Uses proton CLI wrapper to profile python -m sglang.bench_offline_throughput
Proton config: --context shadow --data tree --hook triton
Workload matches vLLM: --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 8
All params configurable via CLI args
Output goes to profiling_output/comparison/sglang/offline/
Validates .hatchet output files with proton-viewer
Script runs successfully and produces valid .hatchet files

userStories.title: vLLM online serving profiling script
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want to profile vLLM under online serving conditions with varying request arrival rates.
acceptanceCriteria: Script at scripts/profiling/comparison/vllm_online.sh
Activates ~/vllm/.venv before running
Starts vLLM server with vllm serve and --profiler-config JSON enabling Proton
Uses REST API (/start_profile, /stop_profile) to control profiling window
Runs vllm bench serve with --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 50 --seed 42
Tests at 2 request rates: 1 req/s and 4 req/s (--request-rate flag)
Output goes to profiling_output/comparison/vllm/online/
Cleans up server process on exit using trap
Script runs successfully and produces valid .hatchet files
userStories.notes: Reference existing scripts/profiling/vllm_online.sh for server lifecycle pattern

userStories.title: SGLang online serving profiling script
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want to profile SGLang under online serving conditions with the same workload as vLLM.
acceptanceCriteria: Script at scripts/profiling/comparison/sglang_online.sh
Activates ~/sglang/.venv before running
Starts SGLang server with python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --port 30000
Uses python -m sglang.profiler with --proton --proton-context shadow --proton-data tree --proton-hook triton to control profiling
Runs python -m sglang.bench_serving with --dataset-name random --random-input 1024 --random-output 256 --num-prompts 50 --seed 42
Tests at 2 request rates: 1 req/s and 4 req/s (--request-rate flag)
Output goes to profiling_output/comparison/sglang/online/
Cleans up server process on exit using trap
Script runs successfully and produces valid .hatchet files
userStories.notes: SGLang default port is 30000. profiler.py sends /start_profile POST with proton params

userStories.title: Profile analysis script with proton-viewer
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want to extract and compare kernel-level metrics from all profiles to identify performance differences between vLLM and SGLang.
acceptanceCriteria: Script at scripts/profiling/comparison/analyze.sh
Runs proton-viewer on all .hatchet files from both frameworks
Extracts top-20 kernels by GPU time for each framework and mode (offline/online)
Categorizes kernels by type: attention, MLP/FFN, normalization, embedding, other
Computes aggregate GPU time per kernel category for side-by-side comparison
Saves raw proton-viewer output to profiling_output/comparison/analysis/ as text files
Prints summary table to stdout showing vLLM vs SGLang kernel time breakdown
Handles missing profile files gracefully (warns and skips)
userStories.notes: proton-viewer -m time/ns <file> extracts kernel timing. May need to parse text output for categorization

userStories.title: Detailed comparison report
userStories.description: As a researcher, I want a detailed analysis report with per-kernel comparisons and actionable recommendations.
acceptanceCriteria: Report generation script at scripts/profiling/comparison/generate_report.sh (or .py)
Report output at profiling_output/comparison/report.md
Section 1 — Executive Summary: key findings in 3-5 bullet points
Section 2 — Methodology: model, hardware, workload parameters, profiling config
Section 3 — Offline Batch Comparison: per-kernel GPU time table, total GPU time, kernel count
Section 4 — Online Serving Comparison: per-kernel GPU time at each request rate, scheduling overhead
Section 5 — Kernel Category Breakdown: aggregated time by category with percentage, as comparison table
Section 6 — Memory & Occupancy: any available memory/occupancy metrics from Proton
Section 7 — Observations & Recommendations: what each framework does better, actionable items
Section 8 — Raw Data Appendix: pointers to all profile files and analysis outputs
Report uses markdown tables for all comparisons
Report is self-contained and readable without running scripts
userStories.notes: This story depends on US-005 analysis output. Parse proton-viewer text files to build report tables
